meta.method: Generated from _standards/carriers/mate-rov.json (by_locator): each row is one MATE competency and one standard it draws on, with that competency's own strength and reason.

crosswalk.note: Turning a large real-world challenge into specific requirements.
Explaining why one design was chosen over another, with the trade-offs.
Choosing a fuse trades protection against nuisance trips.
A safety criterion that has to be met before anything else is traded.
Safety is the criterion that outranks the others when trade-offs are judged.
A computer simulation is a natural way to test a controller before the pool.
A hard limit on current is a constraint the design has to be built around and tested against.
Voltage, source and shutdown time are criteria and constraints to design inside.
A conductive, wet operating environment is a constraint on every connection.
The float's power limits are constraints on its design.
The rules are constraints on what a design may do.
The venue's dimensions are constraints that set the design.
Spelling out the criteria and constraints a solution is tested against.
The scoring asks a team to compare two ways of solving the same problem against stated criteria.
Analyzing test data to see what each design does well or badly.
Practice runs are iterative testing, and each run's data improves the next.
